agree.reason: Opening with her own $600K figure, showing a break-even she can check, and dealing with the IT-system worry up front makes a 20-minute call an easy yes for a busy VP.

honest.reason: All the numbers are correct and the weaker result is disclosed, but calling 21% 'our smaller result' hides that only two of six customers track errors and one hasn't shared numbers, so it reads as a floor when it isn't.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $75K annual cost, the roughly 13% break-even against her $600K, and the 21% and 54% reductions, so the weaker case still reads as a clear win.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is implicitly set as $600K a year in returns that keeps going, which matches the facts, but the email never says outright what that costs her each year she waits.

qualification.reason: The 'not every site improves that much' hedge is backed by a real number, but the single-warehouse pilot has no success bar, timeframe or consequence Dana could hold them to.

objections.reason: It meets the IT director's likely objection directly: it doesn't replace the warehouse system, IT can review it first, and they can start with one warehouse. It raises no objection the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It's short, in short paragraphs that read easily on a phone, with a sharp subject line and one clear ask, as the brief wanted.
